issues: First render opened s11 on ~0.28s of blank stock because the first assembly beat landed a stock plate on a stock ground — an invisible event. Fixed by landing the trim frame, plate label and registration bar on that beat.
First render came out at 30fps despite data-fps=24 on the root, because hyperframes_compose passes --fps explicitly and defaults to 30. Fixed by passing fps=24 through video_compose.

audio_spotcheck.levels: mean -16.4 dB, peak -2.3 dB — headroom intact, no clipping

promise_preservation.notes: render_runtime=hyperframes as locked at proposal (d-003). No fallback, no substitution. 12 distinct shots, all motion authored per-shot.

metadata.distinctness_review: Could this be any other product's video? No — the conceit is bound to the source being three printings of one film, and every transition is drawn from how those prints are made. Does it reuse a look built before? No — no stock scene-type, no registry block, no preset playbook; the composition is hand-authored for this piece.
metadata.check_gate: npx hyperframes check: 0 errors, contrast 37/37 pass WCAG AA. Remaining warning is timeline density (12 clips on one track), accepted deliberately — see metadata.density_note.
metadata.density_note: The lint suggests splitting into sub-compositions. Rejected: HyperFrames requires <audio> to be a direct child of the host root and forbids sub-compositions from animating host elements, so splitting would scatter this piece's media and motion across a boundary for readability alone. Monolithic is the lower-risk choice here.
